title: Meet Shashi
answer: Shashikant Chaudhary works across AI, mathematics, research, teaching, and connected hardware. His education combines a B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering with master’s degrees in Mathematics and Computing and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

His work includes personalised learning with LLMs, conversational risk analysis, student learning analytics, firmware and Python tools, and university teaching. Student-facing university roles have also shaped his clear, practical approach to communication.

title: Education and academic foundations
answer: Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, University of Adelaide, completed December 2025. Final CGPA: 6.923/7, with Dean’s Recognition of Academic Excellence. Studies included statistical machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and big data.
Master of Mathematics and Computing, Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, completed August 2023. B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering, BML Munjal University, completed July 2020.

title: University teaching
answer: As a Casual Academic / Teaching Support during 2025–2026, Shashi supported undergraduate and postgraduate tutorials, practical sessions, workshops, assessment, and constructive feedback with course teams.

Across different teaching periods, he supported Mathematics for Machine Learning; Mathematics for Data Analytics A and B; Advanced Topics in AI and Machine Learning; Concepts in Cyber Security; and Mathematics for Data Science. He helped connect mathematical concepts with practical implementation.
He adapts explanations using pictures and small worked examples, checks for understanding, and prepares clear technical notes and feedback.

title: Mathematical AI evaluation
answer: Shashi’s freelance Mathematics Specialist work with Outlier AI began in 2024. He solved higher-order mathematical problems and reviewed AI-generated work for correctness, logical consistency, and clarity.
The emphasis was on checking the reasoning step by step and explaining where a response needed improvement. The portfolio describes the experience without asserting a current employment status.

title: Skills with evidence
answer: His core combination is Python and data workflows, mathematical reasoning, machine learning, and clear technical communication. Project and coursework tools include pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Git, and Jupyter.

Hardware work adds Arduino firmware, Python device control, MQTT, and monitoring interfaces. SQL is described as coursework/project familiarity. Teaching and student services provide evidence of communication, careful records, and follow-through.

title: Six projects to explore
answer: The portfolio covers six projects: edTuned; Hermes Watcher; OULAD student success analysis; conversational risk analysis; GovNav; and ARBD1’s board-to-dashboard tools.
Each case study explains the problem, Shashi’s contribution, and where to find the repository, publication, or demos. Ask me about any project by name for a closer look.

title: Hermes Watcher: an agent on the desk
answer: Hermes Watcher connects Hermes Agent to a SenseCAP Watcher so agent activity and requests for input are visible on a physical device. The bridge uses Python, MQTT, and embedded C firmware.

The agent runs on the computer; the Watcher displays its status. Approval stays in chat. The project includes a setup guide and validation notes, rather than claiming the model runs on the small device.

title: OULAD: understanding student success
answer: Shashi combined seven linked Open University Learning Analytics Dataset tables, covering 32,593 student records and 10,655,280 interaction records, to explore withdrawal and failure prediction.

His work included validation, cleaning, joins, weekly activity aggregation, feature engineering, and modelling. Repeatable Python scripts and row/key checks helped keep the data workflow consistent. The associated manuscript is in preparation, not a published result.
He kept raw files unchanged, checked row counts and totals after joins, and documented activity-trend and submission-timing features. Settled exploratory logic was moved into reusable Python code.

title: edTuned: personalised learning
answer: edTuned explores LLM-based personalised learning through tutoring agents, adaptive content, and learning pathways. It grew from capstone work and startup exploration, including mentoring through ThincLab.

The project connects AI experimentation with questions about how individual learners can be supported. It is presented as exploration, without claims of commercial scale, paying users, or proven learning outcomes.

title: Published conversational risk research
answer: Shashi co-authored “Conversational Risk Analysis: Identifying and Classifying Potential Threats in Interpersonal Communication.” The Springer chapter was first published online on 1 October 2025 in the CSCT 2024 proceedings.

The work compares machine learning and deep learning approaches using text and audio. His thesis-related contribution involved data preparation, text cleaning, label imbalance, model comparisons, and interpretation. The co-authors are Bansal, Bharadwaj, Panchineni, Suddala, and Chaudhary.

title: GovNav: service navigation
answer: GovNav is a Team SPYDER GovHack prototype exploring AI-assisted government service navigation and plain-language guidance. Shashi contributed as part of the team.
The portfolio presents the prototype and team repository, without claiming government deployment or an unverified award.

title: ARBD1: board to dashboard
answer: During his January–April 2020 technical internship at Hatchnhack, Shashi worked on an Arduino-based educational board: firmware, a Python hardware-control library, and a GUI for monitoring sensors and controlling actuators.
The work connected device readings to a dashboard using MQTT, with Git for collaboration. The Playground includes three recordings showing the board and desktop interface in action.

title: Deep learning reports and code
answer: Three completed Deep Learning Fundamentals assignments are available: perceptron/diabetes-risk classification; CNN image classification on CIFAR-10; and recurrent networks for time-series forecasting.
Each has a description, the actual report, and an implementation repository. Only these three approved deep learning assignments are published.

title: Assignment 1: classification
answer: Shashi built and evaluated a perceptron on the Pima diabetes dataset, then explored sigmoid activation, cross-entropy loss, and class weighting. He compared precision, recall, and F1 with logistic regression, SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost.
This is coursework about classification and evaluation, not a clinically validated diagnostic system.

title: Assignment 2: image classification
answer: Shashi designed a custom PyTorch CNN and compared it with ResNet-18, MobileNetV3, and AlexNet on CIFAR-10. He used Optuna, augmentation experiments, and per-class error analysis to explore generalisation and efficiency.

title: Assignment 3: recurrent networks
answer: Shashi compared RNN, LSTM, GRU, and attention-based LSTM models for next-day Google closing-price prediction. He built 30-day input windows, tuned hyperparameters with Optuna, and evaluated errors on held-out data.
The report is a coursework experiment, without claims of trading performance.

title: University services and operations
answer: Across 2024–2026, Shashi worked in Student Assist, graduation support, health and medical admissions interviews, Succeed@Adelaide, and the English Language Centre.

He handled enquiries and CRM follow-up, supported confidential interview sessions, helped with orientation, and guided international students. The detailed experience page separates the actual roles and responsibilities.

title: Community and leadership
answer: As Joint Secretary of the Thapar Mathematical Society in 2022–2023, Shashi coordinated volunteers, schedules, venues, and faculty communication for events serving more than 200 students.
He organised technology workshops as a Microsoft Learn Student Ambassador in 2019–2020, and completed the University of Adelaide’s five-week Global IQ Connect cultural intelligence program.

title: Beyond the screen
answer: Shashi enjoys hands-on electronics and computing: Raspberry Pi voice-assistant experiments, home automation, server/NAS setups, a DIY speaker, and robotics.
The Playground has six real recordings and two photos, including ARBD1 demos, the Raspberry Pi setup, speaker building, and the electronics workbench.

His personal home lab includes Ubuntu on a Radxa single-board computer, ESP32 sensors, and server/network-storage projects over SSH. He has participated in a line-following robot competition at IIT Delhi and enjoys recreational drone flying.
